dbtForms.branchDescription: This is the branch in your {{provider}} repo that Lightdash should sync to. e.g. main, master or dev
dbtForms.branchDefault: By default, we've set this to main but you can change it to whatever you'd like.
dbtForms.subPathRoot: Put / if your dbt_project.yml file is in the main folder of your repo (e.g. {{example}}).
dbtForms.subPathNested: Include the path to the sub-folder where your dbt project is if your dbt project is in a sub-folder in your repo. For example, if my project was in {{example}}, I'd write /dbt in this field.
dbtForms.subPathFolder: This is the folder where your dbt_project.yml file is found in the {{provider}} repository you entered above.
dbtForms.subPathMainFolder: If your dbt_project.yml file is in the main folder of your repo (e.g. {{example}}), then you don't need to change anything in here. You can just leave the default value we've put in.
dbtForms.subPathSubFolder: If your dbt project is in a sub-folder in your repo (e.g. {{example}}), then you'll need to include the path to the sub-folder where your dbt project is (e.g. /dbt).

github.repositoryFormat: This should be in the format my-org/my-repo. e.g. lightdash/lightdash-analytics
github.connectedDescription: You are connected to GitHub. <accountLink>Click here to use another account</accountLink>

github.hostDomainDescription: If you've customized the domain for your Github, you can add the custom domain for your project in here.

gitlab.tokenScope: Select read_repository scope when you're creating the token.

bitbucket.nativeDescription: Native Lightdash YAML uses Bitbucket Cloud (bitbucket.org).
bitbucket.usernameDescription: This is the login name for your Bitbucket user. This is usually the same username you use to login to Bitbucket.
bitbucket.cloudToken: Bitbucket Cloud requires an <docsLink>API token</docsLink> with Repositories: Read permission. Writeback also requires Repositories: Write and Pull requests: Read and Write permissions.
bitbucket.serverToken: For Bitbucket Server, use an <docsLink>HTTP access token</docsLink> with Project read and Repository read permissions.
bitbucket.nativeSubPath: Folder containing lightdash.config.yml and models/ or lightdash/models/. Use / for the repository root.
bitbucket.hostDomainDescription: If you've <docsLink>customized the domain for your Bitbucket server</docsLink> you can add the custom domain for your project in here.

cloud.generateDocs: The dbt job that builds your project must generate docs.
cloud.refreshAfterJob: After your job finish you need to click the "refresh dbt" button in Lightdash to sync your project.
cloud.serviceTokenDescription: Needs the "Metadata Only" and "Job Viewer" permissions.
cloud.environmentIdDescription: The unique identifier for the dbt production environment, you can retrieve this from the dbt Cloud URL when you navigate to Environments under Deploy.
cloud.webhookDescription: Add this URL as a webhook in dbt Cloud (triggered on job completion) so Lightdash can build a preview when your dbt job finishes.
cloud.webhookSecretDescription: Recommended if you use the dbt webhook above. Paste the secret that dbt Cloud generated for the webhook so Lightdash can verify that incoming requests are genuine. Without it, webhook requests cannot be authenticated.
cloud.discoveryEndpointDescription: Use the endpoint that's appropriate for your <docsLink>region and plan</docsLink>.
cloud.tagsDescription: Only models with all these tags will be synced.

warehouseFields.accountBoundToCliSso: Your CLI SSO connection is bound to this account.
warehouseFields.accountDescription: This is the account to connect to.
warehouseFields.aiAgentMaxBytesBilledDescription: Applies to queries run by AI agents and agent service accounts, before any role limit. Leave empty to use the role or connection limit; 0 means no limit.
warehouseFields.aiAgentQueryLimitDescription: AI agent queries whose dry run estimate is above this are refused, and the agent is told the estimate so it can narrow the query. Dry runs can underreport, so keep maximum bytes billed as the hard limit. Leave empty for no limit.
warehouseFields.assumeRoleArnDescription: Optional IAM role ARN to assume after authenticating. Works with any authentication type.
warehouseFields.assumeRoleExternalIdDescription: Optional external ID for the assume role trust policy.
warehouseFields.assumeRoleExternalIdRequiredDescription: External ID required by the assume-role trust policy, if configured.
warehouseFields.athenaAuthenticationDescription: Choose how Lightdash authenticates to AWS.
warehouseFields.athenaCatalogDescription: This is the Athena data catalog name (typically 'AwsDataCatalog').
warehouseFields.athenaDatabaseDescription: This is the Athena database name (also known as schema).
warehouseFields.athenaRegionDescription: The AWS region where your Athena workgroup is located. See <docsLink>dbt Athena documentation</docsLink> for more details.
warehouseFields.athenaSchemaDescription: This is the schema name (database in Athena).
warehouseFields.audienceDescription: Paste this into the role's trust policy as accounts.google.com:oaud.
warehouseFields.audienceGenerateFailed: Couldn't generate. Select Generate new audience.
warehouseFields.audienceRegenerateWarning: This connection stops working when you save, until the role's trust policy uses the new audience.
warehouseFields.authenticationDescription: Choose how to authenticate with your data warehouse.
warehouseFields.autoCreateUserDescription: Create the database user automatically if it does not already exist (GetClusterCredentials AutoCreate).
warehouseFields.awsAccessPortalUrlDescription: The IAM Identity Center access portal URL users will open to sign in.
warehouseFields.awsAccountIdDescription: The AWS account users should access through IAM Identity Center.
warehouseFields.awsRoleNameDescription: The IAM Identity Center role or permission-set role assigned to users.
warehouseFields.bigQueryAuthenticationDescription: Choose whether to authenticate with a service account or a user account
warehouseFields.bigQueryDatasetDescription: This is the name of your dbt dataset: the dataset in your warehouse where the output of your dbt models is written to. If you're not sure what this is, check out the dataset value you've set in your dbt profiles.yml file.
warehouseFields.bigQueryLocationDescription: The location of BigQuery datasets. You can see more details in <docsLink>dbt documentation</docsLink>.
warehouseFields.bigQueryRetriesDescription: The number of times dbt should retry queries that result in unhandled server errors You can see more details in <docsLink>dbt documentation</docsLink>.
warehouseFields.bigQueryTimeoutDescription: If a dbt model takes longer than this timeout to complete, then BigQuery may cancel the query. You can see more details in <docsLink>dbt documentation</docsLink>.
warehouseFields.bigQueryUrlOverrideDescription: Override the default BigQuery API endpoint. This is useful for Private Service Connect, custom proxies, or local emulators.
warehouseFields.catalogAliasDescription: Name used to attach the DuckLake catalog (defaults to `ducklake`).
warehouseFields.catalogBackendDescription: Database that stores DuckLake catalog metadata.
warehouseFields.catalogFilePathDescription: Path to the catalog database file on the Lightdash server.
warehouseFields.cliSsoChooseWhere: Choose where Lightdash should query, then deploy your project to finish.
warehouseFields.cliSsoDevTitle: Connect with SSO (dev CLI — run from the repo root)
warehouseFields.cliSsoEnterAccount: Enter your account above to generate a code.
warehouseFields.cliSsoIntro: The quickest, most secure way to connect. Run these two commands in your terminal — our CLI signs you into Snowflake in your browser and sets up a secure, revocable connection for you, with no credentials to copy by hand.
warehouseFields.cliSsoWaiting: Waiting for the CLI to finish signing in…
warehouseFields.clusterIdentifierDescription: The identifier of your provisioned Redshift cluster.
warehouseFields.computeDescription: Configure compute resources to use in your models
warehouseFields.confirmQueriesAboveDescription: Users must confirm before running a query whose estimate is above this. Requires query cost estimates. Leave empty for no confirmation.
warehouseFields.connectionStringDescription: If set, takes precedence over account name + key.
warehouseFields.credentialsSourceDescription: Choose whether to use organization-level credentials or configure new credentials
warehouseFields.dataPathDescription: Where DuckLake stores Parquet data files.
warehouseFields.databaseOnboardingDescription: Where your data lives. You can add more later.
warehouseFields.databaseUserDescription: The Redshift database user to request temporary credentials for.
warehouseFields.databricksDocsHint: Check out for more details in <docsLink>given documentation</docsLink>.
warehouseFields.databricksSsoDisabled: Enter server host name to enable Databricks sign-in
warehouseFields.datasetsLoadFailed: Failed to load data sets. You can type manually.
warehouseFields.disableTimestampConversionDescription: When disabled, the connection will skip converting timestamps to UTC. This can improve performance but requires your data to already be in UTC format.
warehouseFields.duckdbSchemaDescription: The default schema for your DuckDB connection.
warehouseFields.ducklakeSchemaDescription: The default DuckLake schema your queries will use.
warehouseFields.endpointDescription: Override for S3-compatible providers (leave empty for AWS).
warehouseFields.executionProjectDescription: You may specify a project to bill for query execution, instead of the project/database where you materialize most resources. You can see more details in <docsLink>dbt documentation</docsLink>.
warehouseFields.externalBrowserConfigured: External browser authentication is configured. Authentication will occur through your default browser when connecting to Snowflake.
warehouseFields.gcpProjectId: This is the GCP project ID
warehouseFields.generateNewCodeHint: Generate a new code and try again.
warehouseFields.hostDescription: This is the host where the database is running.
warehouseFields.identityCenterRegionDescription: The AWS region where IAM Identity Center is configured.
warehouseFields.keepAliveIdleDescription: This specifies the amount of seconds with no network activity after which the operating system should send a TCP keepalive message to the client. You can see more details in <docsLink>postgresqlco documentation</docsLink>.
warehouseFields.keepClientSessionAliveDescription: This is intended to keep Snowflake sessions alive beyond the typical 4 hour timeout limit You can see more details in <docsLink>dbt documentation</docsLink>.
warehouseFields.keyFileDescription: This is the JSON key file. You can see <docsLink>how to create a key here</docsLink>.
warehouseFields.localDataPathDescription: Server-local directory. Only viable for single-pod deployments.
warehouseFields.maximumBytesBilledByRoleDescription: Overrides the limit above for queries run in the app, using each person's highest project role. Leave a role empty to use the limit above; 0 means no limit. Custom roles use the limit above.
warehouseFields.maximumBytesBilledDescription: When a value is configured, queries executed by dbt will fail if they exceed the configured maximum bytes threshold. You can see more details in <docsLink>dbt documentation</docsLink>. Leaving this field empty or with a 0 value means no limit.
warehouseFields.motherduckDatabaseDescription: Your MotherDuck database name, for example `my_db`.
warehouseFields.motherduckSchemaDescription: The default schema in MotherDuck, usually `main`.
warehouseFields.motherduckTokenDescription: Create an access token in MotherDuck Settings.
warehouseFields.noProjectCredentials: No project-level credentials will be used. Users must provide their own credentials to connect.
warehouseFields.organizationCredentialsDescription: Select which organization credentials to use for this project
warehouseFields.passwordDescription: This is the database user password.
warehouseFields.portDescription: This is the port where the database is running.
warehouseFields.postgresSslModeDescription: This controls how dbt connects to Postgres databases using SSL. You can see more details in <docsLink>dbt documentation</docsLink>.
warehouseFields.priorityDescription: The priority for the BigQuery jobs that dbt executes. You can see more details in <docsLink>dbt documentation</docsLink>.
warehouseFields.privateKeyFileDescription: This is the .p8 private key file. You can see <docsLink>how to create a key here</docsLink>.
warehouseFields.privateKeyPassphraseDescription: Optional passphrase for encrypted private keys
warehouseFields.projectAccess: You have access to this project
warehouseFields.projectsLoadFailed: Failed to load projects. You can type manually.
warehouseFields.queryTagDescription: This is Snowflake query tags parameter. You can see more details in <docsLink>dbt documentation</docsLink>.
warehouseFields.queryTimeoutDescription: If a query takes longer than this timeout to complete, then the query will be cancelled.
warehouseFields.redshiftAssumeRoleArnDescription: An IAM role Lightdash assumes to mint Redshift credentials for queries. Not yet supported for dbt compilation. Leave blank to use the host's IAM role (self-hosted), or provide AWS access keys under Advanced.
warehouseFields.redshiftAuthenticationDescription: Choose whether to authenticate with a database username and password, AWS IAM (temporary credentials), or AWS IAM Identity Center (browser sign-in).
warehouseFields.redshiftRegionDescription: The AWS region where your Redshift cluster or serverless workgroup is located.
warehouseFields.redshiftServerlessDescription: Enable if connecting to a Redshift Serverless workgroup rather than a provisioned cluster.
warehouseFields.redshiftSslModeDescription: This controls how dbt connects to Redshift databases using SSL. You can see more details in <docsLink>dbt documentation</docsLink>.
warehouseFields.requireUserCredentials: Require users to provide their own credentials
warehouseFields.requireUserCredentialsInherited: Require users to provide their own credentials follows the primary connection.
warehouseFields.retriesDescription: Number of times to retry failed queries.
warehouseFields.roleDescription: This is the role to assume when running queries as the specified user.
warehouseFields.roleOnboardingDescription: Controls what Lightdash can see. A read-only role is best.
warehouseFields.s3DataDirDescription: S3 location for storing table data (optional).
warehouseFields.s3StagingDirDescription: S3 location for Athena query results.
warehouseFields.schemaOnboardingDescription: We'll start with this schema — you can add more later.
warehouseFields.sdkCredentialChain: Leave blank to use the SDK credential chain.
warehouseFields.sdkCredentialChainDetailed: Leave blank to use the SDK credential chain (IAM role, web identity, …).
warehouseFields.searchPathDescription: This controls the Postgres "search path". You can see more details in <docsLink>dbt documentation</docsLink>.
warehouseFields.secretAccessKeyDescription: Secret access key paired with the access key ID above.
warehouseFields.selectDataset: Type or select a data set
warehouseFields.showQueryCostEstimatesDescription: Runs a free BigQuery dry run before queries in the explorer and SQL runner and shows the estimated bytes processed.
warehouseFields.snowflakeTimeoutDescription: Sets the maximum execution time for queries. If a query takes longer than this timeout, Snowflake will cancel it. This uses Snowflake's STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_IN_SECONDS session parameter.
warehouseFields.snowflakeUrlOverrideDescription: Usually this instance would connect to a default url: account.snowflakecomputing.com. If you'd like to override this (e.g. for the dbt server) you can specify a full custom URL here.
warehouseFields.snowflakeWarehouseOnboardingDescription: The compute Snowflake uses to run queries. A small one is fine for BI.
warehouseFields.sourceDescription: Optional identifier for queries in Trino logs (e.g., project name or team).
warehouseFields.sshPublicKeyDescription: Generate a key and add it to your SSH host before saving.
warehouseFields.sslCertDescription: The client certificate used to authenticate your connection to the database.
warehouseFields.sslKeyDescription: The private key associated with your certificate, required for secure authentication.
warehouseFields.sslRootCertDescription: The trusted certificate authority (CA) certificate used to verify the database server’s identity.
warehouseFields.staticAccessKeyDescription: Advanced: static IAM user access key, only if you are not using an assume-role ARN or the host's IAM role. Long-lived secret — prefer assume-role where possible.
warehouseFields.subject: Subject
warehouseFields.subjectDescription: This Lightdash instance's identity. Use it as accounts.google.com:sub and accounts.google.com:aud.
warehouseFields.threadsDescription: Number of threads for dbt to use.
warehouseFields.trinoSslModeDescription: This controls how dbt connects to Trino database using SSL. You can see more details in <docsLink>dbt documentation</docsLink>.
warehouseFields.trustPolicyDescription: Give this to whoever manages IAM in your AWS account. Paste it in the role's trust policy JSON editor. Don't use the Audience box in the IAM console's role wizard.
warehouseFields.useHttpsDescription: This controls whether to use HTTPS to connect to ClickHouse. You can see more details in <docsLink>dbt documentation</docsLink>.
warehouseFields.usePersonalCredentialsDescription: Signed-in users with personal BigQuery credentials use them instead of the project connection. Other users use the project connection.
warehouseFields.useSshTunnelDescription: Use SSH tunnel to connect to the database.
warehouseFields.userDescription: This is the database user name.
warehouseFields.webIdentityRoleArnDescription: The IAM role Lightdash assumes in your AWS account. Update its trust policy before you test the connection.
warehouseFields.workgroupDescription: The Athena workgroup to use for queries.
warehouseFields.workgroupNameDescription: The name of your Redshift Serverless workgroup.
warehouseFields.requireUserCredentialsFollowsPrimary: Require users to provide their own credentials follows the primary connection.

warehouseValidators.sshPublicKeyRequired: SSH tunnel is enabled but no public key has been generated. Click "Generate public key" and add it to your SSH host before saving.

snowflakeAgentIdentity.description: Your organisation requires agent identity. Agents on this connection run only for people who have connected their agent.

dataTimezone.label: Data timezone
dataTimezone.description: The timezone your warehouse stores ambiguous timestamps in. Defaults to UTC if not set.
dataTimezone.stepByStep: The current moment, step by step
dataTimezone.noTimezone: No data timezone set, so the warehouse reads the bare value in its own session timezone. Pick one above to control it.
dataTimezone.awareNote: If a column already stores a timezone, step 1 is skipped: the moment is already exact (<mono>{{raw}} UTC</mono>) and your data timezone is ignored, so users see <mono>{{rendered}}</mono>.
